Take 2x from both sides: 2x − 5 = 3; add 5: 2x = 8; divide by 2: x = 4. Check: AE = 2(4) + 3 = 11 and BE = 4(4) − 5 = 11. (Halves of different diagonals match only because it is a rectangle; in any parallelogram BE need not equal AE.) So x = 4.

problems.explain: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so ∠AEB = 90°: 6x + 18 = 90. Take away 18: 6x = 72; divide by 6: x = 12. Check: 6(12) + 18 = 90. (The diagonals of a rhombus need not be equal; what is fixed is the right angle where they cross.) So x = 12.

problems.explain: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so ∠DEA = 90°: 9x = 90. Divide by 9: x = 10. Check: 9(10) = 90. (The diagonals of a rhombus need not be equal; what is fixed is the right angle where they cross.) So x = 10.
